06-Giles.observation: Two participants defending concern two — that under-use is the real risk. The first speaks haltingly about already feeling at a disadvantage; the second reaches for the typewriter analogy, and the room doesn't laugh. The note-taker logs: “There is slightly nervous laughter, then a pause.”

05-Ge.label: who gets fired, who gets promoted?
05-Ge.observation: Two participants trading positions on what AI means for entry-level hiring — one framing junior analysts as a generation being 'canceled out,' the other pushing back that it depends on whether a firm cuts headcount or force-multiplies. The note-taker records that during this stretch, “fewer people nod along than on earlier questions.”

transcript_lines.speaker: A
transcript_lines.text: It really depends. What level of expertise do you already have before you're using AI when you enter the field? If you're already an expert, you can use AI in a way that makes you more productive. But you're kind of canceling out a whole generation of junior analysts.

transcript_lines.speaker: B
transcript_lines.text: I'll push back on that. It really depends on how the business looks at it — whether they cut the position to make more money at the same output, or whether they bring in another person and force-multiply with the tool.
